title: Six years up, one year down
lede: Zany Brainy filed with the SEC from its 1999 offering until 2002, and its buyer did so until 2004. Two sets of figures exist for 1996 to 1999: the company’s own, and a later restatement that adds Noodle Kidoodle’s results as if the two had always been one company. We label which is which.

blocks.title: Stores: 16 to 188 to none
blocks.subtitle: Zany Brainy stores at the dates the filings give a count. The February 2001 figure includes 60 former Noodle Kidoodle stores.
blocks.xLabel: Fiscal year end or date of the report (not evenly spaced)

points.title: the first overbuild
points.text: 38 stores opened in three years. The company called the results “disappointing” and changed managers.[^1]

points.title: the IPO year
points.text: 103 stores in 26 states, and the best profit the company made on its own.[^2]

points.title: the peak
points.text: 188 stores in 34 states after the Noodle Kidoodle merger and 27 openings.[^3]

points.title: Chapter 11
points.text: 187 stores on May 15, 2001. All of them went to The Right Start in September.[^5][^10]

points.title: the parent’s bankruptcy
points.text: FAO Inc. closed 80 Zany Brainy stores in its 2003 reorganization and kept 89.[^14]

points.title: liquidation
points.text: FAO Inc. announced on December 2, 2003 that it would liquidate the chain.[^17][^25]

blocks.source: Fiscal 1994–98: prospectus[^1]. Fiscal 1999: annual report[^2]. February 2001: annual report[^3]. May 2001: press release[^5]. Spring 2002 and April 2003: FAO Inc. annual reports[^12][^14]. The final zero is the announced liquidation of all 89 stores[^17][^25]; we have no date for the last closing.

blocks.title: Net sales
blocks.subtitle: $ millions, by fiscal year. Toggle between Zany Brainy’s own figures and the restated figures that include Noodle Kidoodle.
blocks.source: Zany Brainy alone: prospectus and fiscal 1999 annual report[^1][^2]. Restated: fiscal 2000 annual report, which combines the two companies for every year shown because the merger was accounted for as a pooling of interests[^3]. Fiscal 2000 had 53 weeks. Figures are rounded from thousands.

blocks.title: Net income and loss
blocks.subtitle: $ millions, by fiscal year, on the same two bases.
blocks.source: Prospectus and annual reports[^1][^2][^3]. Fiscal 1998 includes a $6.2M net tax benefit (Zany Brainy alone) and fiscal 1999 restated includes a $7.3M tax benefit recorded by Noodle Kidoodle and a $1.6M gain on discontinued operations. Fiscal 2000 includes a $33.9M valuation allowance against deferred tax assets.

blocks.title: What the company blamed for the 2000 loss
blocks.subtitle: Items the annual report names as the main reasons for the $80.7M net loss, $ millions. They overlap with tax effects and do not add up to the loss.

items.label: Charges tied to the Noodle Kidoodle acquisition
items.note: Includes $20.6M of merger and integration costs and an $8.8M inventory write-off.

items.label: Losses from ZanyBrainy.com
items.note: The equity loss in the internet joint venture.

blocks.source: Fiscal 2000 annual report[^3]. The report also names the 10.0% fall in comparable-store sales, which it does not put a dollar figure on as a cause of the loss.

blocks.title: Where the 187 stores went
blocks.subtitle: The stores The Right Start took over in September 2001, by what became of them.

from.label: Stores sold to The Right Start, Sep 2001

to.label: Closed in FAO Inc.’s 2003 reorganization
to.note: Chosen store by store on projected 2003 results[^14]

blocks.source: 187 stores[^10][^11]; “reduced to 169 as a result of closures”[^12]; 80 closed and 89 remaining[^14]. The first figure is derived. FAO Inc.’s fiscal 2002 report describes the same closings as 171 stores acquired, two closed during fiscal 2002 and 80 closed in the reorganization; the totals agree.
